FeaturesPage.title: Advanced 6-Layer Architecture
FeaturesPage.subtitle: How the Graph-Augmented Bayesian Simulation Engine works.

data.name: Layer 1: Ingestion & Data Sources
data.desc: Aggregates internal ad spends, exogenous market intelligence, and consumer transactional logs.

storage.name: Layer 2: Storage & Knowledge Graph
storage.desc: TimescaleDB for time-series logs, Weaviate for embeddings, and Neo4j for semantic relationship mapping.

mmm.name: Layer 3: Bayesian MMM
mmm.desc: Uses PyMC-Marketing to build adstock decay and Hill saturation S-Curves, avoiding the linear budget fallacy.

abm.name: Layer 4: Agent-Based Mesa Engine
abm.desc: 1,000+ autonomous consumer agents simulating exposure, word-of-mouth, and conversion paths.

opt.name: Layer 5: Genetic Optimization
opt.desc: NSGA-II multi-objective genetic algorithms determining the Pareto-optimal budget frontier.

llm.name: Layer 6: Local & Cloud LLMs
llm.desc: Bilingual executive summaries and Cypher natural language querying grounded in Neo4j context.

FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.a1: Bayesian Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) uses PyMC to evaluate ad effectiveness by incorporating prior information and estimating non-linear saturation curves, rather than assuming linear responses.
FAQ.a2: Agent-Based Models (ABM) simulate the actions and interactions of autonomous customer agents to assess how advertising exposures diffuse via word-of-mouth and convert over time.
FAQ.q3: Does the system support offline mode?
FAQ.a3: Yes, for maximum privacy, the platform supports offline execution utilizing a local Ollama instance running Gemma 4.
FAQ.q4: How does GraphRAG prevent AI hallucinations?
FAQ.a4: GraphRAG retrieves exact facts from the Neo4j Knowledge Graph to feed into the LLM system prompt. The model is constrained to write reports based strictly on the retrieved mathematics.
